name: Thanksgiving Turkey Upside Down
subtitle: Denise’s method
equipment: Roasting pan (or foil pan on a baking sheet), roasting rack, meat thermometer, skewer
notes: In only 20 or so easy steps!

items: About ⅓ cup oil, in a small container
About ¼+ cup salt, in a small container
Thickener, about 2 cups (2 parts water to 1 part flour, or 4 parts water to 1 part cornstarch)
Salt, pepper, and chicken bouillon, to taste

steps.title: 1. Buy the turkey
steps.body: Buy enough turkey for leftovers (see recipe below as evidence of need for this).

steps.title: 2. Get a thermometer
steps.body: If you don’t have an electronic thermometer for temperature checks, consider investing in one—this makes all the difference!

steps.title: 3. Thaw the turkey
steps.body: Remember to thaw your turkey in advance—about a day per five pounds in the refrigerator. I also sometimes put the frozen turkey in an ice chest and monitor the temp, keeping the ice chest below 40 degrees. You can thaw faster—check the Butterball site for instructions.

steps.title: 4. Plan the timing
steps.body: On Thanksgiving morning or earlier, determine ETF (estimated time of feasting), calculate the amount of time you’ll need to roast the turkey (about half an hour per 4 pounds of turkey), add 1½ hours to that for prep and resting and carving. Count that amount of time back from ETF to know when you need to begin turkey prep!

steps.title: 5. Clean the prep area
steps.body: Clean your prep area—optimally one side of the kitchen sink and the counter next to it.

steps.title: 6. Ready the pan
steps.body: Pull out your roasting pan and have it ready. If you are using a foil pan, place it on a baking sheet for stability. Also, have your thermometer ready.

steps.title: 7. Prepare the ingredients
steps.body: Prepare the following: **2+ oranges**, sliced thinly; **1–2 bunches celery**, chopped in 2” lengths; **1–2 large onions**, chopped roughly; a small container with about **⅓ cup oil**; a small container with about **¼+ cup salt**; seasoning salt; and a skewer.

steps.title: 8. Preheat the oven
steps.body: Set oven rack on low and preheat oven to 325°F. (Or, if you’re using a roasting oven—a handy thing to free up the oven for other foods—and especially useful if you have a hotel room to plug it in while the family is camping in Death Valley…)

steps.title: 9. Prepare the bird
steps.body: Retrieve your bird and place it in the sink. Remove packaging, and discard. Remove giblets and neck and any paper/packaging from the inside of the turkey. It’s ok to leave the plastic “leg straps” in place—they won’t melt. You can cook the neck and giblets if you like. They make a tasty pet treat. (I usually discard them though.) If the inside of your bird is still frozen, don’t panic.

steps.title: 10. Rinse the turkey
steps.body: Fill the sink with water and slosh water through both “top” and “bottom” bird cavities and rinse outside of turkey. If you are still working to dig out the innards, make the water as hot as you can get it, even running it directly into the cavities, and you may need to change the water a few times until you can loosen the innards. You can sing “Your Baby Has Gone Down the Drain” as you do this.

steps.title: 11. Dry the turkey
steps.body: With the turkey clean and fully defrosted, shake water out of both cavities, place it on the towel, and pat dry.

steps.title: 12. Add the oranges
steps.body: This step sounds creepy, but it’s not that bad...but you need strong fingers. Work those fingers between the skin and turkey flesh to create space for the orange slices—several on the breasts, the thighs, and if possible, on the back. Place oranges in the space you’ve created.

steps.title: 13. Season the cavities
steps.body: Rub the salt into the interior cavities, then stuff lightly with the celery and onions, and use a skewer to secure the fatty skin flap over the “lower” cavity.

steps.title: 14. Set up the turkey
steps.body: With breast side up, rub the turkey with oil and sprinkle generously with seasoning salt. Place the meat thermometer probe in the thickest part of the breast (you can remove the little pop-up thermometer—you can’t see it anyway), secure the drumsticks in the plastic “leg holder”, and flip the turkey onto its breast and into the roasting pan (on the roasting rack if you have one). And yes, this is the upside down part—proven to produce an uglier bird, but much moister breast meat!

steps.title: 15. Oil and season the back
steps.body: Rub the turkey back with oil and sprinkle generously with seasoning salt.

steps.title: 16. Roast
steps.body: Place the turkey in the oven, set the thermometer to 165°F and proceed with other activities. Check in about two hours—if the turkey top is getting brown, cover loosely with heavy foil.

steps.title: 17. Clean up
steps.body: Clean up your working space with soap and water to sanitize for the rest of your feast prep.

steps.title: 18. Rest the turkey
steps.body: Remove turkey when breast temperature reaches 165°F. Let sit for 5–10 minutes before carving—cover the foil with a towel to keep it warm.

steps.title: 19. Move the turkey
steps.body: Move the turkey to a cutting board to free up the drippings for gravy making. Remove any celery and onions. Do your best to separate the fat from the drippings—discard the fat.

steps.title: 19. Brown the drippings
steps.body: Place drippings in a heavy pan (or leave in the roasting pan if it’s not aluminum foil) and brown to desired darkness. Pour about **4–6 cups water** into the drippings and bring to a boil.

steps.title: 19. Thicken the gravy
steps.body: Prepare about **2 cups thickener** (2 parts water to 1 part flour, or 4 parts water to 1 part cornstarch)—whisk together to remove lumps. Drizzle thickener into drippings, whisking as you go, just until the gravy reaches desired consistency. Turn heat off and season with salt, pepper, and chicken bouillon to taste.

steps.title: 20. Carve
steps.body: Carve turkey and enjoy! (The vegetables are tasty, but not very pretty, so I usually discard most of them.)

steps.title: 21. Refrigerate leftovers
steps.body: Make sure to refrigerate all the meat within three hours so you can use it for leftovers. Discard or freeze before about five days.

yields: Plan on about 1½ lb whole turkey per person, more for leftovers (estimated)
